p: The Sandown Industrial Park address gives the game away: you're right by Sandown Park, Esher's famous racecourse. On big race days the roads round here can get busy, so if your visit lands on a meeting day, give yourself extra time to park up and get through the traffic. Esher station sits right next to the course, which is handy if you'd rather come by train from Waterloo.

For a bigger day out, the area is a cracker. Hampton Court Palace is only a short drive away at East Molesey, with Henry VIII's kitchens, the gardens and the famous maze, which is a brilliant follow-on for kids who still have a bit of puff left. Bushy Park, right next door to the palace, has herds of deer roaming free and lots of space for a picnic.

Head the other way and Painshill at Cobham is a restored eighteenth-century landscape garden with a grotto, a Gothic temple and a lake, all made for exploring. Car fans should look up Brooklands Museum in Weybridge, where the old banked motor-racing track still stands and there's a big collection of cars and aircraft to gawp at.

Closer to the trampolines, Esher Common and West End Common are good, free places for a walk among the heather and pines. It's a nice way to cool down, and a dog-friendly option if the family pooch has been waiting in the car (on a cool day, of course). Esher high street has cafés and places to eat, so a post-jump lunch is sorted without going far.
